*Issue Description:* 
`Exception`'s can happen in the {{DataPlane}} Controllers.

{{kubernetes}} handles this by supporting a configurable re-try policy.

If the maximum number of attempts has been passed {{kubernetes}} allows for the Controllers to be informed and take appropriate action.

`v1` had a mechanism to propagate the `Exception` to the `ControlPlane`.

`v2` has no such mechanism.

*Acceptance Criteria:* 
Design and develop a mechanism to propagate `Exception`'s to the {{ControlPlane}}.

items.fromString:
*Issue Description:*
Create a GitHub actions job which would check that the PR is properly formatted before running any other PR check.

Right now all the PR checks run in parallel. Often the PR check contains formatting issue, making all the PR check jobs wasting resources and time, as they all fail in this case.
To save resources we should run a small PR check first, which would check that code is properly formatted and "safe to test" label exists. Once this check pass then all other PR checks should be started.


*Acceptance Criteria:*
* Preliminary PR check checking PR formatting is implemented
* All other PR checks are started once preliminary check pass

*Out of Scope:*

*Additional Information:* 
-Such PR check composing should be possible by using "workflow_run" event as trigger, see https://stackoverflow.com/questions/62750603/github-actions-trigger-another-action-after-one-action-is-completed- Unfortunately this approach doesn't associate triggered job with PR, so the check is not part of PR check.

items.fromString:
*Issue Description:*
Create a GitHub actions job which would check that the PR is properly formatted before running any other PR check.

Right now all the PR checks run in parallel. Often the PR check contains formatting issue, making all the PR check jobs wasting resources and time, as they all fail in this case.
To save resources we should run a small PR check first, which would check that code is properly formatted and "safe to test" label exists. Once this check pass then all other PR checks should be started.


*Acceptance Criteria:*
* Preliminary PR check checking PR formatting is implemented
* All other PR checks are started once preliminary check pass

*Out of Scope:*

*Additional Information:* 
Such PR check composing should be possible by using "workflow_run" event as trigger, see https://stackoverflow.com/questions/62750603/github-actions-trigger-another-action-after-one-action-is-completed

*Issue Description:*

In v2 of our API, Sinks are independent resources on the API. We need to investigate how we wish to model Sinks, what is their lifecycle and how they are then referenced in a Processor.

We also need to consider how we deploy Sinks. The basic idea at the minute is that we simply proxy the RHOC API to create a Sink Connector.

*Acceptance Criteria:* 
 * Investigate and define the API for deploying a Sink resource
 * Define how a Sink resource is referenced by the user in their Camel DSL
 * Define how we deploy Sink Connectors via RHOC

*Out of Scope:* 
 * Implementation. This is to get us to the proposal stage, where we can then discuss implementation plan

items.fromString:
*Issue Description:* 

For the 30 days milestone, we will be allowing the user to express their processing logic in Camel DSL. There will be significant limitations on what the user can do for the 30 days milestone, with the goal being to deliver a Processor API that illustrates the potential of using Camel DSL to express Processing logic. 

At the end of the 30 days milestone, we will conclude with a demo of this functionality.

*Acceptance Criteria:* 
 * Using the RHOSE API, a user can provide a Processor definition using our Camel DSL syntax for simple event matching and routing
 * Using the RHOSE API, a user can provide a Processor definition using our Camel DSL syntax for a content-based routing scenario
items.toString:
*Issue Description:* 

For the 60 days milestone, we will build on our work started in the 30 days milestone and allow the user to express their processing logic in Camel DSL. We will attempt to remove some of the limitations of the 30 days milestone, with the goal being to deliver a Processor API that illustrates the potential of using Camel DSL to express Processing logic. 

At the end of the 60 days milestone, we will conclude with a demo of this functionality tied to a use-case for RHOSE.

*Acceptance Criteria:* 
 * Using the RHOSE API, a user can provide a Processor definition using our Camel DSL syntax for simple event matching and routing
 * Using the RHOSE API, a user can provide a Processor definition using our Camel DSL syntax for a content-based routing scenario
